name: Zambia
summary: Victoria Falls from the side that gets wet, the walking safari where it was invented, the Lower Zambezi by canoe, and parks with almost no traffic in them.
window_alt: Dust and low sun through acacia, a game vehicle on the track
when: Walking safaris run in the dry season; many camps close for the rains.

entries.caption: The Smoke That Thunders
entries.description: Mosi-oa-Tunya: a kilometre and a half of the Zambezi falling into a basalt gorge, and spray you can see from thirty kilometres away.
entries.subject: Victoria Falls in full flood with spray rising from the gorge

entries.caption: The Zambezi Valley
entries.description: Escarpment, floodplain and winterthorn forest, with the river braiding through the middle of all of it.
entries.subject: the Zambezi river and escarpment in the Lower Zambezi valley

entries.caption: Leopard Country
entries.description: The South Luangwa has one of the densest leopard populations in Africa, and the best chance of seeing one hunting.
entries.subject: a leopard in a sausage tree in the South Luangwa valley

entries.caption: The Walking Safari
entries.description: Invented in the Luangwa in the 1950s: no vehicle, an armed scout, and everything at eye level.
entries.subject: a walking safari group and guide in the South Luangwa bush

entries.caption: The Nyika Plateau
entries.description: Two thousand metres of rolling montane grassland on the Malawi border, with roan antelope and no heat.
entries.subject: rolling montane grassland on the Nyika plateau

entries.caption: Victoria and Kalambo
entries.description: Victoria Falls needs no introduction; Kalambo, on the Tanzanian border, drops 235 metres in a single uninterrupted fall.
entries.subject: the single 235 metre drop of Kalambo Falls

entries.caption: Zambezi, Kafue, Tanganyika
entries.description: Three great river systems and the southern tip of Lake Tanganyika, the second deepest lake on earth.
entries.subject: sunset over the Zambezi river with hippo in the shallows

entries.caption: Lake Tanganyika Shore
entries.description: Clear freshwater, sand and forested hills at Nsumbu, about as far from anywhere as Zambia gets.
entries.subject: the clear freshwater shore of Lake Tanganyika at Nsumbu

entries.caption: Miombo and Winterthorn
entries.description: Miombo woodland turning red at the start of the rains, and the winterthorn groves the elephants feed under.
entries.subject: elephants under winterthorn trees in the Lower Zambezi

entries.caption: Devil's Pool and the Gorge
entries.description: Swim to the lip of Victoria Falls in low water, then raft the grade five rapids in the Batoka gorge below it.
entries.subject: rafting the grade five rapids in the Batoka gorge below Victoria Falls

entries.caption: Lozi, Bemba, Tonga
entries.description: Seventy-three ethnic groups, seven official languages, and a royal barge ceremony older than the country.
entries.subject: Lozi paddlers and drummers on the Zambezi floodplain

entries.caption: The Barotse Floodplain
entries.description: The Lozi live with the flood — moving cattle, homes and the king himself when the Zambezi rises.
entries.subject: a Lozi fisherman poling a dugout on the Barotse floodplain

entries.caption: Nshima and Kapenta
entries.description: Maize nshima with relish, dried kapenta from the lakes, and fresh bream out of the Zambezi.
entries.subject: nshima with relish served at a Zambian table

entries.caption: Kuomboka
entries.description: When the floodplain fills, the Litunga is paddled to high ground on the Nalikwanda barge, drummed the whole way.
entries.subject: the Nalikwanda royal barge during the Kuomboka ceremony

entries.caption: Basketry and Copper
entries.description: Tight coiled baskets from the Western Province, and copper worked on the belt that built the economy.
entries.subject: coiled baskets woven in Zambia's Western Province

entries.caption: Livingstone
entries.description: The old colonial capital above the falls, its museum, and the tree where the man himself is said to have camped.
entries.subject: the colonial-era museum building in Livingstone, Zambia

entries.caption: Mosi-oa-Tunya, UNESCO
entries.description: World Heritage since 1989, shared with Zimbabwe, and named by the Kololo long before anyone renamed it.
entries.subject: the knife-edge bridge and gorge at Mosi-oa-Tunya, Victoria Falls

entries.caption: Lusaka
entries.description: The centre of everything: Kabwata market, the Great East Road, and the flights that get you to the parks.
entries.subject: a busy market street in Lusaka

entries.caption: Livingstone's Verandas
entries.description: Corrugated iron and deep colonial verandas along Mosi-oa-Tunya Road, built for heat and never modernised.
entries.subject: a colonial veranda building on Mosi-oa-Tunya Road in Livingstone

entries.caption: Markets and the Great North Road
entries.description: Roadside charcoal and tomatoes, long-haul trucks to the copperbelt, and a bus that leaves when it fills.
entries.subject: a roadside produce market on the Great North Road in Zambia

entries.caption: Village Around the Park
entries.description: Community campsites and craft cooperatives on the Luangwa boundary, funded by the same beds that fill the lodges.
entries.subject: a community craft cooperative near the South Luangwa park boundary

entries.caption: Canoeing the Lower Zambezi
entries.description: Three days downstream past hippo pods and elephant crossings, camping on islands, no engine at any point.
entries.subject: canoeing past elephants on the Lower Zambezi river

entries.caption: Bush Camps, Six Beds
entries.description: Seasonal bush camps in the Luangwa that take six guests, close at the rains, and are walked between.
entries.subject: a small thatched bush camp overlooking the Luangwa river

entries.caption: Kafue and the Carnivores
entries.description: Kafue is the size of Wales; the conservation programmes there fund anti-poaching across the whole Greater Kafue system.
entries.subject: wild dogs on the Busanga plains in Kafue National Park

entries.caption: Luangwa at Last Light
entries.description: The river bends, the hippo surface and the dust goes gold about forty minutes before the drive has to end.
entries.subject: hippos in the Luangwa river at last light

entries.caption: Liuwa Plain
entries.description: The second largest wildebeest migration in Africa, on a plain almost nobody has heard of, reachable only in the dry.
entries.subject: wildebeest massed on the open grass of Liuwa Plain

entries.caption: Wilderness, Still Unmanaged
entries.description: Zambia kept the walking safari, the small camp and the empty park while its neighbours scaled up.
entries.subject: a lone safari vehicle on an empty track in the South Luangwa
